summary: Galena Mountain's 1931 L-4 cab served as an Aircraft Warning post, then moved to Maloney Ridge; footings remain on the mountain, but the road is out.

facts.status_note: Cab moved off the mountain (1941 per the register, 1950 per Willhite); footings are captioned at the site in a 2018 visit.

visit.trail_note: Willhite's notes: climb about 80 vertical feet from the Index-Galena Road; a photo caption dates a washout on that road to 2007-2008; access not yet re-established as of his page.

events.note: L-4 cab; Kresek (cited by Willhite) has the station established by 1931 with an L-4 cab
Cab moved to Maloney Ridge per the register and Weebly; Willhite gives 1950 as the year it was reported moved
Aircraft Warning Service post with observers; activated August 29, 1942
Aircraft Warning Service post deactivated October 7, 1943
Willhite: cab reported to have been moved to Maloney Ridge
Maloney Ridge lookout (its own L-4 cab) removed
Willhite visit, March 2018: no road to the site; three footings captioned

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Weebly page date the move to Maloney Ridge to 1941. Willhite says the cab was reported moved in 1950. The story gives both dates and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Move date conflicts: 1941 (register, Weebly) vs 1950 reported (Willhite); story presents both. Maloney Ridge register does not say whether its 1941 L-4 cab came from Galena Mountain. Elevation conflicts: register 2,459 ft (750 m) vs Willhite 'Elevation: 1,172 feet'; township conflicts: Weebly 28N-11E-30 vs Willhite 'T23N, R11E'. Record location and elevation not changed; a human should check. A search summary claimed concrete foundations remain at Maloney Ridge; not verified on a fetched page, so left out. Weebly lists a 1939 Air Warning Service Post No. 42 telephone report under the Galena heading; not tied to this site in the story.
